subject: Northwind: architecture diagram export + technical review (Dedicated sizing / routing / caching)
content:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Simran Kaur <simran@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 28, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Northwind: architecture diagram export + technical review (Dedicated sizing / routing / caching)
Attachments: northwind-redwood-architecture-v3.png (image/png)

Team — attaching the latest diagram export (v3). Before we send to Nina for customer approval, can we do a quick technical pass on:

1) Dedicated sizing callouts (GPU count/type) — do we want to keep it as “Dedicated GPU pool” or specify “8x H100 80GB”?
2) Routing/fallback labels — diagram currently says “policy-based routing + automatic fallback to compatible model variant”. Want to confirm this matches what’s actually configured for Northwind.
3) Caching callout — I have “prefix + KV cache” on the runtime. Is that accurate / too in-the-weeds for a public asset?

Notes / context:
- This is meant for the public case study page + 1-pager.
- Legal is pushing us to keep hardware/model identifiers optional (ranges or generalized statements).
- Also mindful of SUP-3812 last week (p95 spike). I don’t want us to over-claim anything tied to a single window.

If you can reply with edits (or “LGTM”), I’ll incorporate and route to Camila for final.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference


From: Simran Kaur <simran@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 28, 2025 at 9:31 AM
Subject: Re: Northwind: architecture diagram export + technical review (Dedicated sizing / routing / caching)

Reviewed v3.

(1) Dedicated sizing: I’d avoid exact GPU SKU/count in the public diagram. Suggest label:
- “Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity; autoscaling policy)”
If we need a detail for credibility, add footnote in copy (not diagram) like “sized for peak seasonal traffic” vs hardware.

(2) Routing/fallback: Current language is directionally right, but I’d tweak the fallback box to:
- “Fallback to approved model variant (same output schema) when capacity is constrained”
Avoid implying cross-provider failover.

(3) Caching: “prefix + KV cache” is accurate but might read too low-level. Maybe:
- “Caching + continuous batching (lower $/token while meeting latency SLOs)”

One more nit: the arrow from “App” to “Redwood API Gateway” is labeled “chat/completions”. Northwind uses both chat + embeddings in prod; if we’re going public, we should either broaden to “generation + embeddings” or keep it generic (“LLM requests”).

— Simran


From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>, Simran Kaur <simran@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 28, 2025 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: Northwind: architecture diagram export + technical review (Dedicated sizing / routing / caching)

+1 to Simran’s suggestions.

Messaging preference (public-safe):
- Use “Reserved capacity” / “Dedicated GPU pool” instead of naming H100/A100.
- For routing: “policy-based routing (region, tier, latency)” is OK, but let’s not list too many policies. I’d keep it as “policy-based routing + graceful fallback”.
- For caching: “caching + batching” is enough; “KV cache” tends to trigger technical follow-ups we don’t want to manage in a public asset.

Also can we add a tiny disclaimer line under the diagram (like a caption):
“Diagram is representative; specific model/hardware configurations may vary by deployment.”

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Product Marketing | Redwood Inference


From: Ethan Wallace <ethan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwoodinference.com>, Simran Kaur <simran@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 28, 2025 at 10:26 AM
Subject: Re: Northwind: architecture diagram export + technical review (Dedicated sizing / routing / caching)

From a writing/reader standpoint:

- I like the caption disclaimer Soojin suggested.
- If we keep “fallback” in the diagram, can we ensure the case study body explains it in plain English (ex: “if the preferred deployment is saturated, Redwood automatically routes to an approved variant to keep the feature online”).
- Agree on changing “chat/completions” label to “LLM requests (generation + embeddings)”.

Minor: box “Redwood Console” currently says “token metrics + tracing” — can we broaden to “cost/latency breakdown + rollouts + alerts” or is that scope creep?

— Ethan
Ethan Wallace
Marketing | Redwood Inference

Customer context: Nina is generally fine with “Dedicated reserved capacity” language but has been sensitive about anything that implies their exact infra footprint.

If we can get the updated diagram today, I’ll send to Nina with a tight approval ask:
- confirm diagram is accurate at a high level
- confirm we can use her title + company name with the quote (separate from this thread)

Thanks all — I’ll make the following edits and re-export:

Diagram edits (v4):
- Replace “8x H100 80GB” callout with “Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity + autoscaling policy)”
- Change “chat/completions” arrow label to “LLM requests (generation + embeddings)”
- Replace “prefix + KV cache” with “caching + continuous batching”
- Update fallback label to “Fallback to approved model variant (same output schema) when capacity is constrained”
- Add caption disclaimer: “Diagram is representative; configurations may vary by deployment.”

Console box: I’ll adjust to “cost/latency breakdown + rollouts + alerts” (still accurate and matches our story).

Camila — once I send v4, can you sanity check it against the current outline before Avery forwards externally?

— Markus


From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@northwindcommerce.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Oct 29, 2025 at 11:03 AM
Subject: Re: Northwind: architecture diagram export + technical review (Dedicated sizing / routing / caching)

Avery/Markus — reviewed the updated diagram you sent over.

High-level flow looks correct, and I appreciate keeping the infrastructure details generalized.

Two minor requests before we sign off:
1) Can you remove “autoscaling policy” from the Dedicated label? We do have burst handling, but we’d rather not commit to terminology in a public artifact.
2) On fallback: please avoid implying any change in response format. Maybe: “Fallback to pre-approved configuration to maintain availability” (no “schema”).

If you make those edits, I can confirm approval via email and we’ll route internally for final brand sign-off.

Thanks,
Nina Patel
VP Engineering, Northwind Commerce
